title: The last two core failures, diagnosed and closed

batchRace.diagnosis: The failure data named the cause itself: observed < 3, 1 >, missing < 2 >. All three batches had been delivered. The test waited for six consumed messages and then read a fixture level list that was filled by an unawaited ContinueWith on each batch task, so one append had not run when the assertion executed.
batchRace.fix: The fixture now keeps the batch tasks and the test awaits them. The consumer completes its task inside Consume, before the message is observed as consumed, so every delivered batch is present by construction rather than by timing. The assertion is unchanged.
batchRace.verified: 5 of 5 green in isolation and green in three consecutive full runs.

killSwitchCycles.howItWasFound: The wait helper threw a bare TaskCanceledException, which said nothing. It now reports the status that was reached and the per check entries, and it logs how long each transition took. That turned the next failure into a finding.

underLoad: stayed at Degraded, entry vicione-servicebus-bus=Degraded, for the full 15 s

killSwitchCycles.diagnosis: Not slowness. The first three transitions are instant even under load. The bad messages still queued when the endpoint stops are consumed again after the restart and trip the kill switch anew, so the scenario needs one restart cycle per trip. The log of the failing run contains three 'Kill Switch stopped endpoint' entries for 20 consumed exceptions. At five seconds per cycle that is exactly the fifteen seconds the health wait allows, so the case sat on the edge and fell over it under load.
killSwitchCycles.fix: The restart timeout of this scenario is one second, which is what the sibling spec in the same project and the ActiveMQ spec already used. The container variant and the RabbitMQ one were the only two left at five seconds. Nothing else changed: same thresholds, same message counts, same assertions, same fifteen second budget. Three cycles now cost three seconds instead of fifteen.
killSwitchCycles.alsoFixed: The spec built a ServiceProvider with BuildServiceProvider(true) and never disposed it, so every run left a bus, its timers and the kill switch behind for the rest of the process. It is disposed now.
notDone: No timeout was extended. The fifteen second health budget is unchanged.
No assertion was relaxed, no ordering loosened and no test filtered.

sampling.what: WaitForHealthStatus samples every 50 ms instead of every second.
sampling.why: A caller could wait almost a full second after the status had already flipped, and this spec calls the helper four times. The budget is unchanged and a status that never arrives still expires, so faster sampling can hide nothing.
sampling.effect: The isolated spec went from 10.39 s to 5.78 s.

result.coreRuns: Three consecutive full runs, 1837 of 1837 each.
result.before: Every run failed exactly one of the two cases, a different one each time.
